body:
Fixes #320

## Summary

- Run the bash tool through `command-stream` 1.3.0 instead of `child_process.spawn`. The dependency now owns process signaling, the 200 ms grace period, and output streaming.
- Combine the caller's abort signal with the existing capped timeout through `AbortSignal.any`. Preserve live metadata updates, truncation, timeout and abort messages, and the tool result shape.
- Add a patch changeset for the next release. Remove the dependency-refresh changeset already included in version 0.26.7 so the one-changeset CI check passes. The command-stream 1.3.0 and `fast-uri` dependency updates arrived through the merge with `main`.

## Reproduction and tests

Before the implementation, `bun test ./tests/tool_bash.js` passed five behavior tests but failed the import assertion: `bash.ts` still imported `child_process` and did not import `command-stream`. After the change, all six tests pass. They exercise stdout/stderr, exit metadata, incremental metadata updates, 30,000 character truncation, timeout termination of a child process, and caller abort termination of a child process. The process-tree fixtures are in `experiments/issue-320/`.

`experiments/issue-320/compare-shell.mjs` compares the previous Node shell call with the new command runner for sequences, pipelines, redirection, `cd`, a loop, globbing, and environment expansion; all eight results matched locally.

Local verification:

```text
npm run check                                 passed
npm test                                      802 passed, 4 existing todo, 0 failed
bun install --frozen-lockfile                 passed
bun test ./tests/tool_bash.js                 6 passed, 0 failed
npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high  passed (2 low advisories remain)
node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs          passed
```

## Related process use audit

The other direct `child_process.spawn` under `js/src` is in `session/prompt.ts`, which runs a command through a login shell and has its own streaming logic. The other `Bun.spawn` call sites audited here run narrow executable or protocol commands (Bun, ripgrep, grep, formatter, auth helper, browser opener). Migrating the session shell is a separate follow-up to avoid changing its login setup in this PR.

## Upstream dependency gap

`command-stream` 1.3.0 sends signals to a process and its negative PID but has no Windows process-tree termination path. Node documents that negative PIDs cannot kill a process group on Windows. I reported the gap with a child-heartbeat reproduction in [command-stream#205](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/issues/205) and opened [upstream PR #206](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/206). The upstream regression tests failed on Windows before its fix and now pass, with all upstream checks green. This PR's timeout and abort tests still fail on Windows against the released 1.3.0 package. It needs the upstream fix to be published, then its dependency and lockfiles updated, before this PR can pass on Windows.
